page: Vultr vbm-128c-2048gb-amd is a bare-metal dedicated server configured with 128 physical cores and 256 execution threads powered by AMD EPYC 7713 processors based on the x86_64 architecture operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The platform is provisioned with 2048 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 8 GB per execution core. Dedicated hardware execution ensures that all processing resources remain free from virtualization overhead and neighbor contention.

Storage is provided by a 960 GB local solid-state drive (SSD). The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and operates without dedicated hardware graphics accelerators. The primary local storage footprint is relatively modest compared to the extensive 2 TB memory array, meaning that deployments with massive persistent storage demands will typically leverage auxiliary storage or remote data tiers.

The 1:8 core-to-memory ratio positions this bare-metal platform within the memory-optimized server category. Cost efficiency is achieved via dense hardware consolidation, packing 128 physical cores and substantial memory capacity onto a single bare-metal chassis to eliminate multi-node network latency and reduce per-socket virtualization licensing costs. This server is suitable for large in-memory databases, private virtualization hypervisors, caching layers, and high-concurrency scientific computing.
description: Vultr vbm-128c-2048gb-amd is a bare-metal dedicated server engineered for memory-intensive enterprise tasks. Powered by AMD EPYC 7713 processors on the x86_64 architecture, the machine supplies 128 physical cores and 256 threads operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz, backed by an extensive 2048 GB memory pool with 8 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is configured with a 960 GB local SSD, and networking includes a complimentary public IPv4 address without discrete GPU acceleration. Because hardware access is fully dedicated without hypervisor virtualization layers, processing and memory throughput operate with minimal overhead. The server delivers substantial resource density, maximizing multi-threaded compute efficiency across a unified large-memory footprint. This architecture is well matched for massive in-memory databases, comprehensive hypervisor hosting, in-memory data analytics pipelines, and large-scale batch processing environments that demand high thread concurrency and expansive operational memory.
